newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria State Savings Bank head to resign.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria State Savings Bank head to resign.

text.p: Bistra Dimitrova, chairman of Bulgaria's State Savings Bank (SSB) will resign by the end of the week, the government press centre said.
"Bistra Dimitrova said after a meeting with Prime minister Ivan Kostov she would submit her resignation by the week's end. Kostov said he was satisfied with this decision," the centre said.
Dimitrova was not immediately available for comment.
Earlier on Wednesday Ivan Kostov, the leader of the reformist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) was elected as Prime Minister following his coalition's victory in April 19 general elections.
Dimitrova's appointment as a SSB chairman in June 1995 sparked heated debates in the previous Socialist-dominated parliament.
Deputies from the UDF, then in opposition, alleged that she was linked to powerful private business conglomerates.
SSB, Bulgaria's largest savings institution, operates under a special law and performs most banking activities although it is not a universal bank. It is banned from operating in foreign currency.
Its chairman is nominated by the government and the parliament votes on it. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
